newsitem.title: UK: Europe domestic equity fund inflows jump in April.
newsitem.headline: Europe domestic equity fund inflows jump in April.

text.p: Net flows into European domestic equity mutual funds bounced back in April to an estimated $3.6 billion after slowing in March, according to a report by JP Morgan.
It said the figure was almost double the March intake, and followed a return to net subscriptions in French domestic equity SICAVs of 0.7 billion francs from redemptions of 0.5 billion in March.
French fixed income funds showed no signs of recovery and suffered another month of net redemptions, the report said.
It said net subscriptions by UK funds in domestic equities rose to 955 million sterling from 723 million in March, supported by strong subscriptions to Personal Equity Plans (PEPs).

Overall, UK mutual funds had a record April by bringing in net subscriptions of 2.1 billion sterling. New investment in international equity funds totalled 669 million sterling and bond funds attracting 474 million.

JP Morgan said German interest in international equities remained significant, although was slower in March. In the first three months of the year German mutual funds attracted 9.3 billion marks into this sector.

Net subscriptions to domestic equities in Italy slowed to 23 billion lira -- a six month low. International equity funds in Italy took in 744 billion lira, while fixed income funds held up well in taking in another four trillion lira.
The report said Spanish and Swedish domestic equity funds continued to enjoy strong domestic support, with Spain's 187 billion peseta take the second highest on record.
In Sweden, it estimated the net flow into domestic equities from January to March at 18 billion crowns. This is in contrast to international investors which have been net sellers of Swedish shares.
